title: Find Initial and Final Angular Velocities
text: Based on the knowledge of the Earth and the definition of angular velocity, we know that the initial angular velocity is $$\omega_{i}=\frac{2\pi}{24\,\text{h}}=7.27\times10**{-5}\,\text{rad/s}$$ while the final angular velocity is $$\omega_{f}=\frac{2\pi}{28\,\text{h}}=6.23\times10**{-5}\,\text{rad/s}$$.

title: Kinematics of Rotational Motion
text: Based on the formula $$\omega_{f}=\omega_{i}+\alpha{}t,$$ we see that $$t=\frac{\omega_{f}-\omega_{i}}{\alpha}.$$ To get $$t, $$ first calculate the angular acceleration $$\alpha$$ using $$\tau=I\alpha, $$ where $$\tau=Fr$$ is the torque and $$I=\tfrac25mr**2$$ is the moment of inertia of the Earth (a solid sphere). Use the Earth’s mass $$5.97\times10**{24}\,\text{kg}$$ and radius $$6.378\times10**{6}\,\text{m}$$.
